key_insight: OSReward standardizes how to evaluate reward models for computer-using agents across platforms, aiming to make judge models more reliable and comparable. The core idea is to move from ad hoc verification to a consistent evaluation framework for CUA trajectories.
problem_solved: Computer-using agents need accurate verification of whether they completed user instructions, but human annotators and handcrafted verifiers do not scale. Existing VLM-based judges are promising, yet the field lacks a standardized way to evaluate them across different platforms and tasks.
method: Defines a cross-platform evaluation setting for CUA reward models and trajectory judging.
Organizes CUA trajectories around actions, states, and reasoning to test whether task completion can be verified consistently.
Introduces standardized benchmarks or protocols so different reward models can be compared fairly.
impact: This matters because better reward-model evaluation directly improves agent training, data curation, and deployment safety. For practitioners, OSReward can help identify which judge models are trustworthy before using them in reinforcement learning or automated quality control.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing CUA trajectory -> reward model judge -> task completion verdict
Side-by-side comparison chart of human annotation, rule-based verification, and VLM judges
Cross-platform grid icon set representing different operating systems/apps
Benchmark score dashboard showing standardized evaluation metrics
paper_title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
paper_authors: Qiushi Sun, Kanzhi Cheng, Yian Wang, Bowen Yang, Hang Yan
